studies.Title: Boron intake and prostate cancer risk.
studies.Reference: Boron intake and prostate cancer risk.
studies.comparison_type: highest versus lowest quartile of total boron intake

extraction_supporting_text.sample_size: A total of 35,244 men completed the baseline supplement and food frequency questionnaire (FFQ) in 2000-2002.
extraction_supporting_text.cases: A total of 832 men developed prostate cancer from baseline to 31 December 2004.
extraction_supporting_text.effect_size: The hazard ratio of prostate cancer for those in the highest versus lowest quartile of total boron intake was 1.17
extraction_supporting_text.comparison: those in the highest versus lowest quartile of total boron intake
extraction_supporting_text.design: We evaluated the association between boron intake and prostate cancer within the VITamins And Lifestyle (VITAL) cohort.
extraction_supporting_text.timing: completed the baseline supplement and food frequency questionnaire (FFQ) in 2000-2002
extraction_supporting_text.ethnicity: A total of 35,244 men completed the baseline supplement and food frequency questionnaire (FFQ) in 2000-2002.
extraction_supporting_text.exposure_measurement: A boron database was constructed from published sources to estimate boron intake from the FFQ and from multivitamins.
